statement: The nullspace N(A) consists of all solutions x to Ax = 0, including x = 0. Its vectors have n components and lie in R^n.

anchors.quote: The nulspace N(A) consists of all solutions to Ax= 0.
contains all solutions x to Ax = 0. This includes x = 0.

name_en: The nullspace is a subspace of R^n
statement: If x and y solve Ax=0 then so do x+y and cx, so the solution vectors form a subspace; the nullspace N(A) is a subspace of R^n.

anchors.quote: Since we can add and multiply without leaving the nullspace, it is a subspace.
The nullspace $N ( A )$ is a subspace of $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$ .

statement: Elimination reduces A to its row echelon form R and then finds the special solutions to Ax=0; this finds all solutions and identifies the nullspace.

anchors.quote: Elimination will find all solutions and identify this very important subspace.
The two key steps of this section are

statement: After elimination the columns of R split into pivot columns (containing pivots) and free columns (no pivots). The free components correspond to columns with no pivots.

anchors.quote: Elimination on A produces a row reduced R with pivot columns and free columns.
The free components correspond to columns with no pivots.

statement: The unknowns split into pivot variables (determined by the reduced equation) and free variables (chosen freely). Pivot variables sit in pivot columns, free variables in free columns.

anchors.quote: The pivot variables $x _ { 1 }$ and $x _ { 2 }$ are determined by the equation U x = 0
Three pivot variables $x _ { 1 } , x _ { 2 } , x _ { 6 }$ Four free variables $x _ { 3 } , x _ { 4 } , x _ { 5 } , x _ { 7 }$

statement: Elimination brings A to the upper triangular row echelon form U carrying the pivots; for rectangular A elimination does not stop at U.

anchors.quote: When A is rectangular, elimination will not stop at the upper triangular U.
Elimination (from A to U to R) does not change the nullspace

statement: R = rref(A) is reached by producing zeros above the pivots and dividing to make all pivots equal 1; its pivot columns contain the identity.

anchors.quote: The reduced row echelon form  $R = rref(A)$  has all pivots = 1, with zeros above and below.
The pivot columns of R contain I.

statement: The rank of A is the number of pivots, denoted r. The final matrix R has r nonzero rows.

anchors.quote: The rank of A is the number of pivots. This number is r.
The final matrix R will have r nonzero rows.

statement: For each free column there is a special solution to Ax=0 with that free variable set to 1 and the other free variables 0. The nullspace is all combinations of the special solutions.

anchors.quote: The nullspace of A consists of all combinations of the special solutions to $A x = 0 .$
Every free column leads to a special solution. That free variable is 1, the others are 0.

name_en: There are n - r special solutions
statement: There are n - r free columns, so Ax=0 has n - r special solutions; the complete solution to Ax=0 is a combination of these n - r special solutions.

anchors.quote: The complete solution to $A x = \mathbf { 0 }$ is a combination of the n - r special solutions.
Number of pivots = number of nonzero rows in R = rank r. There are n - r free columns.

name_en: A short wide matrix has a nonzero nullspace
name_zh: 短宽矩阵有非零零空间
statement: If A has more columns than rows (n > m) there is at least one free variable, so Ax=0 has at least one nonzero special solution.

anchors.quote: With $n > m$ there is at least one free variable.
Then $A x = 0$ has nonzero solutions.
Every matrix with m < n has nonzero solutions to Ax = 0 in its nullspace.

statement: N(A) denotes the nullspace of A, the subspace of R^n of all solutions to Ax=0.

anchors.quote: That line is the nulls pace $N ( A )$ . It contains all solutions
The nullspace  $N(A)$  in  $R^{n}$  contains all solutions x to Ax = 0.

statement: R = rref(A) denotes the reduced row echelon form of A.

anchors.quote: $R = rref(A)$  has all pivots = 1, with zeros above and below.

statement: U denotes the upper triangular row echelon form of A reached by elimination.

anchors.quote: elimination will not stop at the upper triangular U.
Elimination (from A to U to R) does not change the nullspace:  $N(A) = N(U) = N(R)$ .
